model_summary: Binary x[w,t] assigning 5 workers to 4 tasks; each task exactly one worker, each worker at most one; minimize total hours.
type_rationale: All variables are 0-1 assignment variables; objective and constraints linear.

model_summary: Integer order counts from A, B, C (15/10/10 chairs per order); 100<=chairs<=500; binaries link 'A used -> >=10 chairs from B' and 'B used -> C used'; minimize chair cost.
type_rationale: Order counts are integer (stated) and the if-then conditions use 0-1 variables; everything linear.
notes: Cost interpreted as per-chair price times chairs per order. Optimum orders only from C; the logical conditions are inactive.

model_summary: Binary x per item (dogs as one indivisible 6000 lot, three diamonds separate) assigning to son 1 or 2; minimize |V1-V2| via epigraph variable d>=+-(V1-V2).
type_rationale: Binary item-allocation variables; objective is an absolute value of a linear expression, minimized, so exactly linearized with a continuous epigraph variable.
notes: Total estate value is odd in thousands so a zero difference is impossible. COPTPY mention ignored; CBC used as required.

model_summary: Continuous flows supply->station and station->demand, binary station-open z_k; supply <= a_i, demand met exactly, station throughput <= q_k z_k, flow conservation at stations; minimize transport + fixed costs.
type_rationale: Continuous shipment quantities plus 0-1 fixed-charge station variables; linear.
notes: Demand modeled as equality; >= would give the same optimum since costs are positive.

model_summary: Preemptive goal programming: integer regular/overtime production of A and B, deviation variables for profit>=10000, contract minimums, Process I =150 h, Process II regular 70 h fully used, overtime <=30 h; priorities solved lexicographically.
issue_note: The problem only asks to 'formulate the model' for goals p1-p4 without stating a single numeric objective. Reading 1: preemptive goal programming (objective = total unmet deviation, all goals attainable -> 0). Reading 2: maximize weekly profit with all goals as hard constraints.

readings.reading: Lexicographic goal programming P1>P2>P3>P4, objective = sum of remaining deviations
Maximize profit with goals p1-p4 imposed as hard constraints (regular Process II exactly 70 h, overtime <=30 h)

type_rationale: Production units integer, deviation variables continuous; all goal constraints and objectives linear.
notes: Overtime units modeled separately with reduced unit profit (280 and 425). In reading 1 the final lexicographic solution is not unique. Reading 2 is the same with integer or continuous production.

model_summary: Integer area (100 m2 units) for contracts (start month s, length k); monthly coverage equals demand exactly; binaries for contract used/length used; >=2 lengths, not both 1- and 4-month, <=3 distinct contract types; minimize rental fee.
issue_note: (a) 'Each contract must cover consecutive months starting from the beginning of the period': read literally (all contracts start in month 1), exact coverage of 1500/1000/2000/1200 is infeasible. (b) Rule 4 'number of distinct warehouse contracts <= 3': as distinct (start,length) contracts it is infeasible with exact coverage; as distinct contract lengths it is redundant and the model is feasible. Main reading: contracts may start in any month, rule 4 counts distinct lengths.

readings.reading: Contracts start any month; rule 4 = at most 3 distinct contract lengths
Contracts start any month; rule 4 = at most 3 distinct (start,length) contracts

type_rationale: Integer contract quantities and 0-1 logic variables; constraints and objective linear.
notes: Integer and continuous areas give the same optimum in the main reading.

model_summary: Continuous kg x[raw,brand]; raw-material monthly limits; ratio constraints on raw A and C content per brand, linearized by multiplying through by brand total; maximize sales minus processing and raw-material cost.
type_rationale: Continuous kg quantities; percentage constraints linear after multiplying by total; linear objective.
notes: Optimum produces no brand C. Reported value contains tiny float noise (6160).

model_summary: Integer units on each device x_k <= cap_k*y_k with binary setup y_k; total 2000 units; minimize setup + unit production costs.
type_rationale: Product units are integer and device-enable variables are 0-1; fixed-charge linear model (MILP if units are treated as continuous).
notes: Continuous units give the same optimum.

model_summary: Continuous start times with precedence constraints; T >= all finish times; minimize 1000*T + 5000*(finish B - start A).
issue_note: 'The cost of work per day is 1000 Euros': read as per day of project duration (main) or per activity-day of work (constant over all schedules).

readings.reading: Work cost 1000 per day of project duration
Work cost 1000 per activity-day (sum of durations, constant)

type_rationale: Continuous start times and makespan; linear precedence constraints and linear cost.
notes: Durations fixed (no crashing); project starts at time 0.

model_summary: Continuous x[i,j] bought in quarter i and sold in quarter j>=i (10^4 m3); sales <= max sales; warehouse capacity 20 on all stock held in each quarter; storage cost 70+100u yuan/m3 for u>=1 quarters; maximize profit (10^4 yuan).
issue_note: Two unclear points: (1) whether the 200,000 m3 capacity limits all timber in the warehouse in a quarter (including timber bought and sold in the same quarter) or only inventory carried to later quarters; (2) whether storage cost a+b*u applies with u=0 to timber sold in the purchase quarter. Also the table header says 10,000 m2, read as 10,000 m3.

readings.reading: Capacity on all stock held each quarter; storage cost only for u>=1
Capacity only on inventory carried to later quarters; storage cost only for u>=1
Capacity on all stock; storage cost a+b*u also charged for u=0

type_rationale: Continuous purchase/sale/storage quantities; linear constraints and objective.
notes: Objective in units of 10^4 yuan. With the stated storage cost (>=170 yuan/m3 per quarter stored) carrying inventory is never profitable, so the result depends only on the readings above.

model_summary: Binary x[part,machine] and setup y[machine]; each part on exactly one machine; x1A + x2A = 1; parts 3,4,5 fixed to A,B,C; at most 3 parts on C; minimize processing + setup costs.
type_rationale: All variables 0-1; the if-then condition between parts 1 and 2 becomes the linear equation x1A + x2A = 1.

model_summary: Integer units of A and B; 12A+25B <= 1800 minutes; 5B >= 2A; maximize 3A+5B.
type_rationale: Product units integer; linear constraints and objective (LP if units treated as continuous).
notes: Problem says only 'formulate'; objective assumed to be maximize total profit. Integrality uncertain (textbook may intend LP).

model_summary: Continuous tons of crude A/B in gasoline I/II; crude A purchase split into three price tiers (10000/8000/6000) with ordering binaries because the cost is concave; A available = 500 + purchase, B = 1000; min A share 50%/60%; maximize revenue minus purchase cost.
type_rationale: Continuous quantities; purchase cost is a concave piecewise-linear function of the purchase amount, linearized exactly with tier variables plus 0-1 ordering variables.
notes: Existing inventories treated as sunk (no cost); no processing costs given.

model_summary: Binary arc selection forming a simple directed path A->E through C (flow conservation + MTZ); continuous z <= bandwidth of each selected arc (big-M = max bandwidth); maximize z. Cross-checked by enumerating all simple paths.
type_rationale: Path arcs are 0-1; the objective max of min bandwidth over selected arcs is linearized exactly with an epigraph variable and big-M; result MILP.
notes: Table asymmetric; arcs read as directed row->column. Treating links as undirected with the larger of the two directional values gives the same maximum.

model_summary: Continuous quantities of each food; protein, carbohydrate and calorie minimums; minimize cost.
notes: Main model continuous (servings divisible); if food quantities must be integer the optimum is 24.0 (printed as INTEGER_VERSION in the output). integer_relaxed_objective equals the main value because the main model is already continuous.

model_summary: Continuous quantities of each food; protein, carbohydrate and calorie minimums; minimize cost.
notes: Main model continuous (servings divisible); if food quantities must be integer the optimum is 44.0 (printed as INTEGER_VERSION in the output). integer_relaxed_objective equals the main value because the main model is already continuous.
